Conventional metals like gold and silver have high losses and very large negative real permittivity in the visible and NIR ranges, limiting their plasmonic applications.
Heavily doped wide bandgap oxide semiconductors can exhibit small negative real permittivity and relatively low losses in the NIR.
Transparent conducting oxides (TCOs) such as AZO, ITO, and GZO are promising plasmonic materials in the NIR.
AZO films deposited by pulsed laser deposition at 100°C and 150°C show dielectric functions sensitive to deposition and annealing conditions.
Annealing AZO films at 300°C in forming gas reduces doping efficiency and increases losses.
TCOs provide about an order of magnitude better mode confinement than gold or silver for single-interface SPP waveguides in the NIR.
Propagation lengths of SPPs on TCO/air interfaces are nearly two orders of magnitude shorter than those on gold or silver/air interfaces.
The quality factor (propagation length/mode size) of TCO-based SPP waveguides is about an order of magnitude lower than that of gold or silver waveguides in the NIR.
Metal-insulator-metal (MIM) waveguides with gold or silver have propagation lengths about an order of magnitude longer than TCO-based waveguides with similar mode sizes.
TCO nanoparticles have LSPR quality factors around 2.4 at 2 µm wavelength, enabling NIR plasmonic applications.
Metal nanoparticles like silver and gold have LSPR quality factors of about 6 at 400 nm and 4.5 at 500 nm, respectively.
Hyperbolic metamaterials made from AZO/ZnO layered structures have significantly higher figures-of-merit in the NIR compared to metal/dielectric HMMs.
TCO-based HMMs enable broadband singularities in photonic density of states useful for applications like single-photon sources.
TCOs have smaller negative real permittivity values closer to those of dielectrics, making them suitable for transformation optics devices.
AZO exhibits an epsilon-near-zero (ENZ) crossover wavelength in the NIR with a real refractive index as low as 0.2 and an imaginary part around 1.5.
ENZ materials transmit primarily normally incident waves, with AZO having an acceptance angle of about 18° for a λ/10 thick slab.
Achieving high carrier concentration (~10^21 cm^-3) in AZO is essential for negative permittivity but challenging due to defects and doping efficiency.
ITO films tend to be amorphous with higher carrier scattering compared to polycrystalline AZO films.
Indium is expensive and scarce compared to zinc, motivating research focus on AZO over ITO.
TCOs can be doped to higher levels than many other semiconductors like silicon, enabling metal-like optical properties in the NIR.
